items.followUp: Define a molecule and a cation.

rubric.why: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an atom as the smallest particle of an element.

rubric.why: An ion is an atom or group of atoms that has a net electric charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an ion is a charged atom or group of atoms.

modelAnswer: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction.
An ion is an atom or group of atoms that carries a net electric charge.

items.followUp: Differentiate between electron affinity and ionization energy.

rubric.why: Electron affinity describes the energy released when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.description: States the meaning of electron affinity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating electron affinity to the energy released when an electron is added to a gaseous atom.

rubric.why: Electronegativity is an atom's tendency to attract the shared electrons in a chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the attraction of shared electrons by an atom in a bond.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom.
Electronegativity is the ability of an atom in a chemical bond to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.

items.followUp: State the modern periodic law and identify the property used to arrange elements in the modern periodic table.

rubric.why: Mendeleev's periodic law relates the properties of elements to their atomic masses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses.

rubric.why: The modern periodic law relates the properties of elements to their atomic numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

modelAnswer: Mendeleev's periodic law states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses.
The modern periodic law states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

items.followUp: Why are gases much more compressible than liquids?

rubric.why: Gas particles are separated by much larger spaces than particles in liquids.
rubric.description: Compares the spacing of particles in gases and liquids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gas particles are much farther apart or have larger spaces between them than liquid particles.

rubric.why: The large spaces mean gases contain less mass in a given volume, so their density is lower.
rubric.description: Links particle spacing to lower gas density.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that gases have less mass per unit volume and therefore lower density than liquids.

modelAnswer: Gas particles are much farther apart than particles in liquids, with large empty spaces between them.
Therefore, gases have less mass per unit volume and a lower density than liquids.
